Subtitle

Date: 28 October 2026. The page is Gross Profit table. It shows a week that was already saved. Opening it does not call OpenRoad. Donald Smith’s $0.07 R&M and the 5.5–12 miles-per-gallon band are in this code. They are not on the live site until this code is deployed. W42 and W43 do not change until those weeks are generated again.
1. The week
Heading1
A settlement week is Tuesday through Monday. Week 1 of a year is the Tuesday–Monday week that contains December 28 of the previous year. OpenRoad dates are read in America/Chicago.
2026 week 42 is 6 October through 12 October. 2026 week 43 is 13 October through 19 October.
The page opens on the previous completed week, not the week that is still in progress. The week and year can be changed on the page. Week numbers run from 1 to 53.
2. When a week is built
Heading1
There are two ways a week gets into the database.
Every day at 3:00 AM Eastern, before any report
Heading2

This fills the database the report reads. In order: Prepass tolls, pay setups, drivers, users, trucks, loads, every driver route, truck assignments, then load financials. One failed OpenRoad call does not stop the rest. The Tuesday report reads this database and pulls the Gross Profit pieces again.
Fuel-card files come in on their own import, about every 30 minutes, from the fuel file drop. They are not part of the 3:00 AM list.
Tuesday job
Heading2

Every Tuesday at 5:00 AM Eastern, in this order: Samsara miles per gallon, link fuel-card rows to drivers, Relay fuel, then the report. The report itself pulls again, in this order: pay setups, loads, driver routes for this week, driver routes for the previous week, load financials for this settlement week, fuel-card linking again, Relay again if a Relay key is set, Samsara miles per gallon again. Then it calculates every card and replaces the saved week. If the report step fails, that Tuesday pipeline is marked failed. If Relay has no key, Relay is skipped and older Relay numbers stay.
Running the report by hand does the same two phases. With no dates, it builds the previous completed week. It can also be given one year and week, or a range of weeks in the same year.
Saving a week deletes every saved row for that year and week, then inserts the new rows. A hand edit on that week is wiped when the week is generated again.
A missing recent week
Heading2

If one of the last 6 completed weeks has no saved rows, the app can build it from data already in the database. That path pulls load financials, links fuel cards, and pulls Samsara miles per gallon. It does not pull loads, routes, pay, or Relay again. Then it calculates and saves. Oldest missing week first.
3. Who gets a saved card
Heading1
Only a driver whose status is active. A row is saved when at least one of these is true:
The driver has fuel-card gallons or dollars dated in the Tuesday–Monday week.
b
The driver has miles or gross from the load rules in section 6.
b
The driver has a Prepass toll in the week.
b
The driver has an accessorial whose settlement week is exactly this Tuesday and Monday.
b
The driver type is owner operator or leased owner, a truck is assigned that overlaps the week, and the name is not “test”, does not contain “example”, and does not start with “accounting”.
b
The name is Alvydas Peciulis, Manpreet Singh, or Chevarres Smith.
b
A company or contract driver with no loads, no fuel, no tolls, and no accessorials is not saved, even with a truck assigned.
Name checks use the first word and the last word. A middle name does not block a match.

The truck unit on the card is the latest assignment that overlaps the week: assignment start on or before Monday, and assignment end empty or on or after Tuesday. If several trucks overlap, the latest start date wins.
4. What the page shows
Heading1
The menu item is Gross Profit, then Gross Profit table. A person sees it only when their login is allowed that module.

The filter defaults to Company driver. That filter includes company drivers and contract drivers, and it leaves out Alvydas Peciulis, Manpreet Singh, and Chevarres Smith. The Owner operator filter includes owner operator, leased owner, and those three names. Any other type is its own filter and also leaves those three names out. Only active saved rows are shown. Cards are ordered by driver name. Five cards sit on each row. Export downloads the same layout as an Excel file named Gross-Profit-W week-year.
The header shows the driver name and the truck unit. If there is no unit, it shows a dash.
Green cells can be typed. Enter or leaving the cell saves. Escape puts the old number back. A blank edit is ignored. A number that is not finite, or is below 0, or is 100,000,000 or more, is ignored.

Dollars on the right of an expense line use a dollar sign. A negative amount is shown in parentheses with no dollar sign. Totals always use a dollar sign, including a negative total. Gross profit is green when it is 0 or above, and red when it is below 0. Mileage on the right is shown with up to one decimal. Rate is shown with two decimals, or a dash when miles are 0.

Trip count is calculated and saved. It is not printed on the card. There is no fleet total row. The only count on the page is how many driver cards are showing. If none match, the page says “No fuel or trip data for this week.”
5. Where each input comes from
Heading1
OpenRoad pay setup
Heading2

Three statuses are recognized, and the words must match exactly: Per Mile, Percentage, Flat. Any other status pays $0 before accessorials. Per Mile stores a loaded-mile rate and an empty-mile rate. Percentage stores a keep percent. Flat stores one flat amount.
OpenRoad loads
Heading2
Miles, empty miles, linehaul, revenue, delivery time, status, the load’s driver, and how many drivers are on the load. The load total is not used for gross.
OpenRoad driver routes
Heading2

Each driver’s loaded miles, empty miles, and the date the route was created. The dollar amount on the route is written by our code, described in section 6. It is not taken from OpenRoad as the card gross.
OpenRoad load financials
Heading2

Each driver accessorial has its own sum from OpenRoad. Pay adds those sums for this settlement week. There is no status filter: paid, pending, or any other settlement status is included when the week matches. We do not compute the accessorial as load total minus linehaul. Lumper, storage, miscellaneous, and deduction totals on the load financial record are stored and are not added to driver pay or to gross.
Fuel-card files
Heading2

Gallons, dollars spent, and retail dollars, by transaction date inside the Tuesday–Monday week. A row with no driver is linked by name first (full name, or first and last), then by truck unit while the driver was assigned to that truck.
Relay
Heading2

For the week: retail dollars, paid dollars, diesel gallons, and how many transactions matched the driver. Used for owner-operator fuel, and as a company price-per-gallon fallback. A Relay row is tied to a driver by fuel-card number first, then by first and last name. If the name matches more than one driver, that Relay row is skipped. Unmatched Relay rows are not on any card.
Samsara
Heading2

Miles per gallon for the company fuel cell. You said this should later come from the FMS coaching module. Today it is Samsara. Lookup order for this year and week: the driver id, then a Samsara name that contains this last name and starts with this first name, then a vehicle whose name equals the truck unit.
Prepass
Heading2

Toll charge only. Other Prepass fees are not added. The date is the exit date, or the post date when there is no exit date. It counts only when that date is inside the Tuesday–Monday week and inside the driver’s assignment on that truck. More than one truck in the week is summed.
Configurations
Heading2
Rates that are not from an API. If a rate is saved there, it replaces the default. The defaults in the code are in sections 8 and 9.
6. Shared-load route dollars, before the card
Heading1

This runs when routes are saved, before the card math. Driver count on a load is how many different drivers have a route on that load. If that count is under 2, there is no helper. If it is 2 or more, the helper is a route driver who is not the load’s main driver, and if several qualify, the one with the most loaded miles.
The dollars to split are the load linehaul. If linehaul is missing, load revenue. If the load has no miles, or those dollars are 0, every route on that load is stored with no revenue.
Plain share = linehaul × that route’s loaded miles ÷ the load’s miles, rounded to the cent. Empty miles are not part of this share.

When the load has at least two routes, and the routes’ loaded miles add up to the load’s miles within half a mile, a second rule replaces the plain share. Routes are ordered by position. Every route after the first is floored down to the nearest $100. The first route receives the linehaul minus those floored amounts, rounded to the cent. A proportional $921 can become $1,000 on the first driver and $100 on the next.
When the route miles do not add up to the load miles, each route keeps the plain share. No $100 floor.
The card reads those saved route dollars. It does not split the load a second time.
7. Miles and total gross on the card
Heading1
Total gross is never the load total. Accessorials are never added to gross. A driver can hit more than one case in the same week. The week’s miles and gross are the sum.
Case A — driver count is 0 or 1, and the load has a driver
Heading2
Miles = load miles + load empty miles. Loaded miles = load miles. Gross = linehaul, otherwise load revenue, otherwise 0. Week = delivery date. Canceled loads are left out.
Case B — driver count is exactly 1, and the load has no driver
Heading2

Miles = the route’s loaded miles + empty miles when that sum is above 0. Otherwise, if the load has miles, miles = load miles + load empty miles. Otherwise 0. Loaded miles = the route’s loaded miles when those are above 0, otherwise the load’s miles. Gross = the route revenue when it is not zero, otherwise linehaul, otherwise load revenue, otherwise 0. Week = delivery date. A canceled load is left out only when the route still has miles. A cancel fee with no route miles is kept.
Case C — driver count is 2 or more, and this route driver is not the load’s driver (the helper)
Heading2

Miles = that route’s loaded miles + empty miles. Loaded miles = that route’s loaded miles. Gross = that route’s saved revenue. If that revenue is missing, the code uses the full load linehaul, then load revenue. That fallback can put the whole load’s gross on the helper. Week = the date the route was created, or the route’s updated date if created is missing. Not the delivery date. Canceled loads are not removed.
Case D — driver count is 2 or more, and this route driver is the load’s driver
Heading2

Miles = that route’s loaded miles + empty miles. Loaded miles = that route’s loaded miles. Gross = that route’s saved revenue only. If it is missing, gross is 0. It does not fall back to linehaul. Week = delivery date. Canceled loads are not removed.
Empty miles used in per-mile pay = total miles minus loaded miles, and never below 0.
Rate saved with the week = total gross ÷ miles, or 0 when miles are 0. That saved rate is not rounded. The card prints it with two decimals.
8. Driver pay
Heading1
Per Mile: loaded miles × loaded rate, plus empty miles × empty rate. If the empty rate is missing, the loaded rate is used for empty miles.
Percentage: total gross × keep percent ÷ 100. A keep of 80 means pay = gross × 0.80.
Flat: the flat amount. It is not divided by days or hours.

Accessorials = the sum of amounts whose settlement-week start and end are exactly this Tuesday and this Monday. A negative sum is raised to 0. Pay = the compensation amount plus accessorials, then rounded to the nearest cent.

On a company card, Driver’s pay is an expense line and it is editable. On an owner-operator card, driver pay is still calculated and saved, and it is not shown, and it is not inside owner-operator profit.
9. Company and contract card, line by line
Heading1

Contract drivers use this card. The lines under EXPENSES, in order, are: Driver’s pay, Fuel, PREPASS, Monitoring Logs, R & M, Equipment Lease, Equipment Lease again, Liability insurance, SCALE, Factoring fee, Samsara, Cargo insurance, PD insurance, TOTAL EXPENSES, GROSS PROFIT. Both lease lines are labeled Equipment Lease. The first is $1,054.94. The second is $287.
Fuel
Heading2
Left cell is miles per gallon. Right cell is price per gallon. Both are editable and shown to two decimals.

Miles per gallon: the Samsara figure when it is above 0 and below 1,000. If Samsara has none, miles ÷ gallons. Gallons are fuel-card gallons, or Relay diesel gallons when the card has none. That guess is kept only from 5.5 through 12. Outside that band it is thrown away.
Price per gallon: fuel-card dollars ÷ fuel-card gallons, when gallons are above 0 and the result is 0 or higher. Otherwise Relay paid dollars ÷ Relay diesel gallons, when both are above 0.
Fuel dollars = (miles ÷ miles per gallon) × price per gallon, rounded to the cent. If either number is missing, fuel dollars are the fuel-card spend. Relay dollars are not used as that fallback.

When the page is opened, company fuel is calculated again from the saved miles, miles per gallon, and price per gallon, when both fuel numbers exist. Profit on the screen uses that recalculated fuel. If either fuel number is missing, the screen keeps the saved fuel dollars.
Other company lines
Heading2
PREPASS = the toll total from section 5. It is editable. It is inside company expenses, so it reduces company profit.
b
Monitoring Logs = $41. Not editable.
b
R & M = miles × $0.19. Configurations can replace $0.19. A company R&M change shows up only after the week is generated again. Opening the page does not apply a new company R&M rate to an old week.
b

Liability insurance = miles × $0.15. Configurations can replace $0.15. Same rule: a company change waits for the week to be generated again. No $16 flat on a company card. Rounded to the cent when the week is saved.
b
SCALE = $30.
b

Factoring fee = total gross × the factoring rate. The default in the code is 0.012, which is 1.2%. The sheet header says 0.80%. Configurations can replace it. On a company card, the saved factoring stays until the week is generated again, or until miles or gross are edited by hand.
b
Samsara = $38. This is a fee, not the miles-per-gallon figure.
b
Cargo insurance = $17.50.
b
PD insurance = $162.
b
Company profit
Heading2
Total expenses = driver pay + fuel + Prepass + monitoring logs + R&M + both leases + liability + scale + factoring + Samsara fee + cargo + physical damage.
Gross profit = total gross − total expenses.
Both are rounded to the nearest cent.
10. Owner-operator card, line by line
Heading1
An owner-operator is type owner operator or leased owner, or the name Alvydas Peciulis, Manpreet Singh, or Chevarres Smith. Miles and total gross use section 7. Profit does not.

The card order is: RATE, MILEAGE, TOTAL GROSS IN, XXI Fee, Fuel, then EXPENSES: R & M, Equipment Lease, Liability and cargo insurance, Factoring fee, Samsara, PD insurance, TOTAL EXPENSES, GROSS PROFIT.
The fee label on the screen is “XXI Fee” (one I). The calculation is the XXII company cut.

These are calculated and saved, and they are not printed on the owner-operator card: driver pay, Prepass, monitoring logs ($41), scale ($30), the second equipment lease ($0), and cargo as its own line. Cargo is $0 and is added into the liability line, so that line equals liability.
XXI Fee
Heading2
The percent in the green cell is the company cut, not the driver’s keep. Fee dollars = total gross × fee percent ÷ 100.

If Configurations has a fee percent for that driver, and it is above 0 and below 100, that percent is used. Otherwise the keep percent is used when it is above 0 and below 100. Fee percent = 100 − keep percent. An 80% keep is a 20.00% fee. The percent is rounded to two decimals. If neither percent is usable, the green cell shows the compensation name, or a dash, and the fee dollars are a dash. Profit then has no fee income.
The fee percent from Configurations is applied when the page is opened. It does not have to wait for the week to be generated again.
Fuel
Heading2
Owner-operator miles per gallon and price per gallon are cleared. They are not shown and not used. Fuel sits above EXPENSES. It is not editable on this card.

If Relay has at least one transaction for this driver this week, retail, paid, and gallons come from Relay. Otherwise they come from the fuel-card file. Retail on the card file is the retail amount, or the paid amount when retail is missing.
Most owner-operators: one green number, diesel gallons × $0.12, rounded to the cent. Gallons of 0 means fuel $0.
b

Cheryl Day and Donald Smith: left = retail when retail is above 0, then the higher of retail and paid, rounded to the cent. Right = paid, not below 0, rounded to the cent. Fuel dollars = left − right, not below 0. If retail is 0, fuel is $0.
b

Robert Wagner: left uses that same retail rule. Add-on = gallons × $0.20, rounded to the cent. Right = paid + add-on, rounded to the cent. Fuel dollars = left − right, not below 0. If retail is 0, fuel is $0.
b
Chevarres Smith: fuel is $0.
b
Other owner-operator lines
Heading2

R & M = miles × $0.04, except Donald Smith, whose R&M is miles × $0.07. Configurations can change the $0.04. It does not change Donald Smith’s $0.07. On the owner-operator page, R&M is recalculated from the current rate when the page is opened.

b
Equipment Lease = −$35, unless Configurations sets another amount for that driver. A negative lease shows in parentheses.

Owner-operator profit
Heading2
Total expenses = R&M + equipment lease + liability + cargo + factoring + Samsara fee + physical damage (only when physical damage is above 0).
Gross profit = fee dollars + fuel − total expenses.
Fuel is added. It is not inside total expenses.
Left out of this profit: driver pay, Prepass, monitoring logs, and scale.
Both totals are rounded to the nearest cent. Opening the page recalculates them from the current Configurations rates. Company cards do not do that for R&M, liability, or factoring.
11. What a typed edit recalculates
Heading1

Miles. Rounded to the cent. Rate = gross ÷ miles, rounded to 4 decimals, and the card still prints two. R&M and liability are recalculated from the new miles and rounded to the cent. Factoring is recalculated from the existing gross and rounded to the cent. Company fuel is recalculated when both miles per gallon and price per gallon exist. If either is missing, company fuel stays at the fuel dollars already stored. Owner-operator fuel is not recalculated. Driver pay is not recalculated. Profit is recalculated.

Total gross. Rounded to the cent. Rate is recalculated. Factoring is recalculated and rounded to the cent. If a keep percent above 0 is stored, driver pay becomes gross × that percent ÷ 100, even on a card that was not Percentage, because the edit only checks that a percent is stored. Owner-operator fee is recalculated from the new gross. Miles, fuel, R&M, and liability stay as they are.
Driver’s pay. Company cards only. Rounded to the cent. Company profit uses the new pay. Owner-operator profit does not use driver pay.

Miles per gallon or price per gallon. Company cards only. When both are present, fuel = (miles ÷ miles per gallon) × price per gallon, and profit is recalculated. Clearing either one leaves fuel at the last fuel dollars. A miles-per-gallon value must be above 0 and below 1,000. A price per gallon must be 0 or higher and below 100.
PREPASS. Company cards only. Rounded to the cent. Company profit subtracts it.
12. Configurations screen
Heading1
Company: R&M dollars per mile (default 0.19), liability dollars per mile (default 0.15).
Owner-operator: R&M dollars per mile (default 0.04), liability dollars per mile (default 0.15), liability flat dollars (default 16), equipment lease dollars (default −35).
Factoring is entered as a percent. Default 1.2, stored as 0.012.
Per owner-operator driver: XXII fee percent, equipment lease dollars, PD insurance dollars, liability credit dollars.
Company lease amounts, monitoring logs, scale, Samsara fee, cargo, and company physical damage are not on that screen. They are the fixed amounts in section 9.
13. What is saved on each row
Heading1

Year, week, driver id, name, status, type, unit, compensation name, keep percent, trip count, rate, mileage, gross, driver pay, fuel, fuel retail, fuel paid-side, miles per gallon, price per gallon, Prepass, monitoring logs, R&M, both leases, liability, scale, factoring, Samsara fee, cargo, physical damage, total expenses, gross profit.
The XXII fee percent from Configurations is not its own saved column. It is read from Configurations when the page opens.
